previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented with left arm pain due to worsening steal syndrome in his left brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula. He underwent elective fistula banding the following day, which was successful in reducing blood flow to alleviate symptoms while preserving access function. He remained asymptomatic postoperatively with no neurovascular deficits. His potassium was elevated at 6.4 on admission but decreased after an extended hemodialysis session. He tolerated a regular diet, maintained baseline functional status, and was discharged in stable condition to an extended care facility. Follow-up was arranged with transplant surgery and sleep medicine. Home medications were resumed, and discharge instructions included monitoring for arm symptoms, weight changes, and dialysis access issues.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man s/p banding on ___ of LUE AV fistula still
with significant steal while on dialysis. // Please assess arterial
vasculature flow in patients left arm, has LUE brachiocephalic arteriovenous
fistula.

COMPARISON:  Av fistulogram performed ___

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and Dr.
___ radiology attending) performed the procedure. The
attending, Dr. ___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
75 mcg of fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 75 min during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored by an
independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and
subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl
CONTRAST: 155 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 19 min 6 sec, 54 mGy

PROCEDURE:  1. Left subclavian arteriogram.
2. Left brachial arteriogram.
3. Left radial arteriogram
4. Left ulnar arteriogram.
5. Left brachial and radial arteriogram with compression of fistula.
6. Left brachial arteriogram after intra-arterial nitroglycerin.
PROCEDURE DETAILS:
Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and alternatives to the
procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the patient. The patient
was then brought to the angiography suite and placed supine on the exam table.
The left upper extremity and right groin were prepped and draped in the usual
sterile fashion.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol.
 Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery
was punctured using a micropuncture set at the level of the mid-femoral head.
A 0.018 wire was passed easily into the vessel lumen. A small skin incision
was made over the needle. Then the inner dilator and wire were removed and a
___ wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The micropuncture
sheath was exchanged for a 4 ___ sheath which was attached to a continuous
heparinized saline side arm flush.
The ___ wire was exchanged for an angled glidewire. A 4 ___ angled
glide catheter was advanced along the glidewire to the level of the left
subclavian artery. Hand injection of dilute contrast confirmed position. The
glidewire was removed and digital subtraction images were acquired with
findings detailed below. The glidewire was reintroduced and the catheter was
advanced into the brachial artery, the glidewire removed and a DSA run was
performed demonstrated brisk initial filling of the brachial, radial and
interosseous arteries but with minimal opacification of the vessels the on the
distal forearm. The glidewire was reintroduced and the catheter was advanced
into the radial artery, the glidewire removed and a DSA run was performed.
Again there was decreased filling of the distal vessels with contrast
identified in incomplete ___ arch and no filling of the digital vessels.
The glidewire was reintroduced and the catheter was withdrawn slightly and
advanced into the ulnar artery, the glidewire removed and a DSA run was
performed.  No filling of the distal forearm or hand vessels identified.
The catheter was withdrawn to a level just beyond the brachiocephalic AV
fistula arterial anastomosis. The fistula was occluded and a repeat DSA run
was performed. The findings were unchanged compared to above. Following this
50 mcg of intra-arterial nitroglycerin was administered and a repeat DSA run
was performed.  Again the findings are unchanged.

FINDINGS: 

1. No arterial inflow abnormality identified in the subclavian or brachial
arteries.
2. Decreased filling of the distal radial and ulnar arteries which persisted
after occlusion of the fistula and administration of intra-arterial
nitroglycerin.

IMPRESSION: 

No structural lesion identified to explain the symptoms of steal syndrome. 
Decreased filling of the distal branches and connections of the radial ulnar
arteries despite fistula occlusion and administration of intra-arterial
nitroglycerin.

EXAMINATION:  VENOUS MAPPING FOR DIALYSIS ACCESS

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with ESRD on HD with L BC AV fistula, pain in
hand during HD, planning to switch access to left. // venous mapping of R arm
for dialysis access planning

TECHNIQUE:  Real-time grayscale and Doppler ultrasound imaging of both
cephalic veins, radial artery, brachial artery, basilic vein and subclavian
veins was performed.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

RIGHT:
The cephalic vein is thrombosed in the upper arm but is patent throughout the
remainder of the arm. The cephalic vein measures 0.09 cm at the distal
forearm, 0.11 cm at the mid forearm, 0.14 cm at the antecubital fossa, 0.10 cm
at the mid arm.

The basilic vein measures 0.36 cm at the antecubital fossa, 0.30 cm at its mid
portion, and 0.27 cm at the proximal portion.

The radial artery measures 0.24 cm. The brachial artery measures 0.46 cm.
Arterial calcifications are present in the radial artery.  No calcifications
identified within the brachial artery.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Patent rightbasilic veins.
2. The cephalic vein is thrombosed in the upper arm.
3. Normal respiratory variation in the bilateral subclavian veins. No evidence
of central stenosis.

INDICATION:  Has a history of a left arm fistula with increasing pain. Had a
fall 2 weeks ago. Evaluate for humerus fracture.

TECHNIQUE:  AP and lateral views of the humerus and forearm were obtained with
a total of 4 exposures.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS: 

There is periosteal reaction and callus formation around the shaft of the mid
humerus, consistent with a healing subacute nondisplaced fracture. Alignment
is normal. No other fracture is identified. There is no joint effusion in the
elbow.  Minimal degenerative changes are present in the elbow with small
spurs. There are vascular calcifications.  The soft tissues are otherwise
unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

Subacute healing nondisplaced fracture through the shaft of the left humerus.

NOTIFICATION:   The findings were discussed by Dr. ___ with Dr. ___ on the
telephone on ___ at 1:40 ___, 5 minutes after discovery of the findings.
